title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving emergency Unconditional Cash Transfers to vulnerable populations in Xudur District

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtZamzam Foundation proposes to deliver lifesaving unconditional cash assistance to 1420 of the most vulnerable households in Xudur District, Bakool Region, in response to the worsening drought and escalating food insecurity affecting rural communities. The intervention aligns with the Somalia Humanitarian Fund Reserve Allocation priorities and Food Security Cluster guidance, targeting households experiencing acute consumption gaps, erosion of coping capacities, and heightened protection risks. The project will provide Unconditional Cash Transfers valued at USD 55 per household per month for a duration of three months, covering approximately 70% of the Minimum Expenditure Basket in line with FSC standards.ltbrgtThe assistance will enable crisis-affected households to meet immediate food needs, stabilize consumption, and reduce reliance on negative coping strategies such as distress asset sales, meal reduction, and harmful survival mechanisms. Targeting will prioritize households in IPC Phase 3 and above, with particular focus on female-headed households, families with malnourished children, persons with disabilities, and households hosting displaced populations. Vulnerability-based targeting and verification will be conducted in close coordination with district authorities, community leadership structures, and Food security cluster guidance to ensure transparency, inclusivity, and accuracy.ltbrgtImplementation will be closely coordinated with health and nutrition partners operational in Xudur District. Strong operational linkages will be maintained with partners delivering nutrition interventions such as mass MUAC screening, community-based identification and referral of acutely malnourished children and pregnant and lactating women, outpatient and inpatient treatment of severe acute malnutrition, and supplementary feeding for moderate acute malnutrition. This coordinated approach will ensure that cash assistance complements service delivery, reduces financial barriers to access, and supports continuity of care for vulnerable households.ltbrgtProtection and gender mainstreaming will be embedded throughout the intervention. Targeting and implementation will prioritize women, girls, older persons, and persons with disabilities, and will actively mitigate risks of exclusion, exploitation, and harm. Cash assistance will be delivered in a manner that preserves dignity, safety, and informed choice, with attention to intra-household dynamics and risks of gender-based violence. Referral pathways will be activated for households identified with protection concerns, in coordination with specialized protection and GBV service providers operating in the district.ltbrgtAccountability to affected populations will be central to implementation. Zamzam Foundation will establish and maintain accessible, confidential, and safe feedback and complaints mechanisms, including community-level feedback channels and referral pathways. Beneficiaries will be informed of their entitlements, selection criteria, and available complaint mechanisms through community sensitization and information sharing. All feedback and complaints will be documented, tracked, and responded to in a timely manner. ltbrgtThe key project activities will include: conducting vulnerability-based targeting and household verification registering eligible households and establishing secure beneficiary databases compliant with data protection standards delivering multipurpose cash transfers through approved financial service providers using agreed transfer values and modalities conducting routine post-distribution monitoring to assess timeliness, adequacy, utilization, and beneficiary satisfaction and undertaking regular market monitoring of key food commodities included in the Minimum Expenditure Basket to inform transfer value adequacy. These activities will ensure adaptive management, safeguard accountability, and reinforce the effectiveness of the cash response. ltbrgtlt/pgt
